experiment: Study of Colour Sensor - Question Bank
description: Comprehensive 50-Question Physics Question Bank for Study of Colour Sensor (TCS3200)

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a colour sensor?
questions.explanation: Colour sensors quantify spectral reflectance/emission across RGB wavelengths to classify target chromaticity.

questions.question: RGB stands for:
questions.explanation: RGB represents the additive primary color channels in optoelectronics and trichromatic vision.

questions.question: Which component is commonly used to detect light?
questions.explanation: Photodiodes generate current proportional to the flux of incident photons on their p-n junction.

questions.question: Which RGB colour has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Red light occupies the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum (~620–750 nm).

questions.question: Which RGB colour has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Blue/violet light has the shortest wavelength in visible spectrum (~400–495 nm).

questions.question: If a surface reflects mostly red light, it generally appears:
questions.explanation: An object's apparent color is determined by the spectral bands it reflects into the detector.

questions.question: Visible light is a part of:
questions.explanation: Visible light consists of electromagnetic waves in the frequency range ~430–750 THz.

questions.question: The approximate visible-light wavelength range is:
questions.explanation: Human and sensor visible spectral sensitivity spans roughly 380/400 nm (violet) to 700/750 nm (deep red).

questions.question: A photodiode converts incident light into an:
questions.explanation: The photoelectric effect creates electron-hole pairs, producing a measurable photocurrent or voltage.

questions.question: Equal high RGB intensities ideally produce:
questions.explanation: Additive mixing of full-intensity Red, Green, and Blue produces White light.

questions.question: Very low RGB intensities correspond approximately to:
questions.explanation: The absence of reflected or emitted light (R=G=B≈0) corresponds to Black.

questions.question: Red plus green light produces:
questions.explanation: In additive color synthesis, Red + Green = Yellow.

questions.question: Green plus blue light produces:
questions.explanation: In additive color synthesis, Green + Blue = Cyan.

questions.question: Red plus blue light produces:
questions.explanation: In additive color synthesis, Red + Blue = Magenta.

questions.question: The unit nm commonly represents:
questions.explanation: 1 nanometer (nm) = 10⁻⁹ meters, standard for optical wavelengths.

questions.question: A sensor is a device that:
options: Detects a physical quantity and produces a usable signal
questions.answer: Detects a physical quantity and produces a usable signal
questions.correct_option: Detects a physical quantity and produces a usable signal
questions.explanation: Transducers/sensors convert physical stimuli into readable electrical responses.

questions.question: A colour sensor mainly detects:
questions.explanation: Colour sensors measure electromagnetic radiation in the visible band.

questions.question: If a surface absorbs most visible light, it appears:
questions.explanation: High absorption with minimal reflection reflects almost no photons back to the sensor.

questions.question: Which region is normally detected by a visible colour sensor?
questions.explanation: Visible sensors have optical filters calibrated for human visual bandwidths (400–700 nm).

questions.question: The three common colour channels in an RGB sensor are:
questions.explanation: TCS3200 uses an 8x8 array of photodiodes partitioned with Red, Green, Blue, and Clear filters.

questions.question: Why are multiple RGB channels useful?
options: They allow different spectral components to be compared
questions.answer: They allow different spectral components to be compared
questions.correct_option: They allow different spectral components to be compared
questions.explanation: Comparing relative filter responses lets the system differentiate hue and saturation independently of light intensity.

questions.question: If the red-channel reading is much higher than green and blue, the target has a strong:
questions.explanation: High red filter transmittance indicates abundant photons in the ~650 nm wavelength region.

questions.question: What is the role of an ADC?
options: Convert an analog signal into digital values
questions.answer: Convert an analog signal into digital values
questions.correct_option: Convert an analog signal into digital values
questions.explanation: Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) quantize continuous photocurrent voltages into discrete digital numbers.

questions.question: Why is calibration important for a colour sensor?
options: It improves accuracy and accounts for system variations
questions.answer: It improves accuracy and accounts for system variations
questions.correct_option: It improves accuracy and accounts for system variations
questions.explanation: Calibration normalizes for ambient lighting, LED color temperature, detector responsivity offsets, and distance.

questions.question: Why can the same object give different readings under different light sources?
options: Illumination spectrum and intensity can change
questions.answer: Illumination spectrum and intensity can change
questions.correct_option: Illumination spectrum and intensity can change
questions.explanation: Reflected spectrum = Incident spectrum × Reflectance curve. If the source spectrum changes (e.g. tungsten vs sunlight), reflected light changes.

questions.question: Why should sensor-to-target distance often be kept constant?
questions.explanation: Light intensity obeys the inverse-square law; varying distance shifts signal amplitudes.

questions.question: What is spectral response?
options: Variation of sensor output with wavelength
Variation of resistance with length only
questions.answer: Variation of sensor output with wavelength
questions.correct_option: Variation of sensor output with wavelength
questions.explanation: Spectral responsivity R(λ) defines the output current per watt of incident optical power as a function of wavelength.

questions.question: Which is most directly related to colour rather than just brightness?
questions.explanation: Ratios r = R/(R+G+B) isolate chromaticity (hue/saturation) from luminance.

questions.question: If all RGB readings rise by roughly the same proportion, what likely changed?
questions.explanation: Scaling all color channels uniformly indicates a change in light source brightness or distance, not color.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a white reference surface?
options: Provide a known response for comparison/calibration
questions.answer: Provide a known response for comparison/calibration
questions.correct_option: Provide a known response for comparison/calibration
questions.explanation: A high-reflectance white standard (like barium sulfate or PTFE) provides full-spectrum reference calibration.

questions.question: Why can ambient light affect a colour sensor?
options: It adds unwanted light to the measured signal
It stops the sensor from detecting red
questions.answer: It adds unwanted light to the measured signal
questions.correct_option: It adds unwanted light to the measured signal
questions.explanation: Stray background photons combine with the target reflection, skewing RGB proportions.

questions.question: What does wavelength describe?
options: Distance between corresponding points of a wave
questions.answer: Distance between corresponding points of a wave
questions.correct_option: Distance between corresponding points of a wave
questions.explanation: Wavelength λ is the spatial period of the optical wave crest-to-crest.

questions.question: Photon energy is related to frequency by:
questions.explanation: Planck-Einstein relation: E = hf = hc/λ, where h is Planck's constant.

questions.question: For electromagnetic radiation in vacuum:
questions.explanation: The wave speed equals frequency times wavelength: c = fλ ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.question: If wavelength increases in vacuum, frequency:
questions.explanation: Because c = fλ is constant, frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength (f = c/λ).

questions.question: Which condition improves repeatability of colour measurements?
questions.explanation: Consistent lighting and fixed sensor geometry guarantee reproducible spectral measurements.

questions.question: RGB values can be normalized mainly to reduce the effect of:
questions.explanation: Normalization converts raw values into chromaticity coordinates r, g, b where r + g + b = 1.

questions.question: A matte surface is often easier to measure consistently because it:
questions.explanation: Lambertian (matte) diffusion scatters light uniformly in all directions, avoiding specular glare spikes.

questions.question: A colour sensor's output is most directly related to:
questions.explanation: The electrical output directly corresponds to the radiant flux captured by the filtered photodiode array.

questions.question: Under additive colour mixing, equal red and green with little blue appears approximately:
questions.explanation: Combining Red and Green spectral emissions stimulates red and green cone photoreceptors, perceived as Yellow.

questions.question: A sensor gives R=200,G=50,B=40 and another gives R=100,G=25,B=20 under identical conditions. Best conclusion:
options: Their relative colour composition is similar but the second signal is weaker
questions.answer: Their relative colour composition is similar but the second signal is weaker
questions.correct_option: Their relative colour composition is similar but the second signal is weaker
questions.explanation: Both maintain a 4:1:0.8 channel ratio, meaning the hue is identical while luminance differs.

questions.question: Why are RGB values not exact wavelength measurements?
options: Each channel usually responds over a range of wavelengths
Each channel detects one exact wavelength
questions.answer: Each channel usually responds over a range of wavelengths
questions.correct_option: Each channel usually responds over a range of wavelengths
questions.explanation: Broadband optical filters integrate photon flux over wide transmission passbands (~50–100 nm FWHM).

questions.question: If the same spectrum is made twice as bright, what should ideally remain similar for colour estimation?
questions.explanation: Scaling intensity doubles numerator and denominator, leaving ratios R/(R+G+B) invariant.

questions.question: Why is ambient-light shielding useful?
options: It reduces unwanted light added to the measured signal
It removes the need for calibration in every system
questions.answer: It reduces unwanted light added to the measured signal
questions.correct_option: It reduces unwanted light added to the measured signal
questions.explanation: Optical hoods prevent room fluorescent/daylight flicker from contaminating the reflected LED signal.

questions.question: If RGB spectral responses overlap, then:
options: One wavelength range can contribute to multiple channels
Each channel detects exactly one wavelength
questions.answer: One wavelength range can contribute to multiple channels
questions.correct_option: One wavelength range can contribute to multiple channels
questions.explanation: Intermediate wavelengths (e.g. 580 nm yellow) pass partially through both Red and Green filter curves.

questions.question: Why is a white reference useful before measuring unknown colours?
options: It provides a baseline for channel responses under the current illumination
questions.answer: It provides a baseline for channel responses under the current illumination
questions.correct_option: It provides a baseline for channel responses under the current illumination
questions.explanation: White balance calibration normalizes channel gains against the true spectral power distribution of the illuminant.

questions.question: If room lighting changes and readings become unstable, the most likely issue is:
questions.explanation: Unshielded fluctuations in ambient room lights contaminate photodiode integration.

questions.question: A dominant red-channel response primarily means:
options: More red-region light is reaching the sensor relative to other channel responses
The surface emits only red photons
The sensor has no green/blue sensitivity
questions.answer: More red-region light is reaching the sensor relative to other channel responses
questions.correct_option: More red-region light is reaching the sensor relative to other channel responses
questions.explanation: Photocurrent from the red-filtered photodiodes exceeds that from green/blue filters.

questions.question: Best way to compare colours when overall brightness varies:
options: Use calibrated or normalized channel values
questions.answer: Use calibrated or normalized channel values
questions.correct_option: Use calibrated or normalized channel values
questions.explanation: Chromaticity normalization removes the scalar dependence on lux/illumination level.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes a colour-sensor experiment?
options: Relating optical response to different colours/light conditions and electrical output
questions.answer: Relating optical response to different colours/light conditions and electrical output
questions.correct_option: Relating optical response to different colours/light conditions and electrical output
questions.explanation: The experiment studies the optoelectronic transduction of spectral reflectance into calibrated RGB frequency/voltage signals.
